articles.title: LeBron James and Savannah James make another impactful contribution to improve educational opportunities for Akron children
articles.summary: NBA News: LeBron James and his wife, Savannah James, have consistently worked towards developing their hometown, Akron, as they continue to be surrounded by fam.
articles.body: LeBron James and his wife, Savannah James, have consistently worked towards developing their hometown, Akron, as they continue to be surrounded by fame and wealth. While the four time NBA champion has focused on getting back to the court for probably his last season with the Philadelphia 76ers, his foundation’s education wing has worked on a meaningful project for children coming from underprivileged families in Akron.LeBron James’ foundation’s education wing makes an impactful addition for the children of AkronA few days ago, the LeBron James Family Foundation’s education wing, the I PROMISE School took to its social media to make a post that read as, “The start of the school year is right around the corner and @leaf_homeandblooms joined us at I Promise School for a professional development experience that offered our teachers a lesson that went far beyond flowers. 🙌”The post added, “As they created their own bouquets, they noticed that even the same flowers weren’t the same. Some had more thorns, some more greenery, and each needed different care. Our students are the same.”The post continued, “Each comes with their own strengths, challenges, needs, and unique ways of growing. Our teachers & staff do an incredible job learning how to continue to give them the care, support, and space they need to flourish.”LeBron James’ childhood acted as an inspiration for his work concerning bridh=ging the education gap in AkronFor close to a decade, the four time NBA champion’s foundation’s education wing, the I PROMISE School has worked extensively to improve education gaps for children coming from modest backgrounds in Akron.A lot of what LeBron James has worked on related to education comes from his own experience when he grew up in Akron.In an interview with ESPN, LeBron James reflected on his childhood as he said, "But any time that I would show up to school, it's weird, the teachers would always tell my mom that when he shows up, he's one of the best students that we have.”The four time NBA champion added, “We just hope that he can show up more. And we just couldn't do it at that point and time. So I know exactly what a lot of these kids are going through."Both LeBron James and his wife, Savannah James, have remained committed to the cause and have raised millions of funds to help children across Akron.Apart from academics, LeBron James has also helped set up accessible healthcare in Akron while actively helping a number of communities through the LeBron James’ Family Foundation.With just a few more days left for the new season to begin, fans are gearing up to watch the NBA icon take the court for one last time.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Rhyne Howard sets WNBA season record for 3-pointers, Angel Reese scores 30 with 10 rebounds as Dream win big over Sun
articles.summary: Howard broke Sabrina Ionescu's season record for 3-pointers, while Reese extended her record for double-doubles in a season.
articles.body:
Rhyne Howard set a single-season record for most 3-pointers made, while Angel Reese scored 30 points and grabbed 10 rebounds in the Atlanta Dream's 103-59 win over the Connecticut Sun on Thursday.

Howard hit her 129th 3-pointer of the season with 6:45 remaining in the fourth quarter to break a tie with Sabrina Ionescu , who set the previous 3-point record during the 2023 campaign.

Angel Reese notches 30th double-double of season

Meanwhile, Reese hit the 30-point mark for the second time this season. She appeared to be on her way to breaking her career high of 31 points, set nearly a month ago against the Phoenix Mercury . Reese had 19 points, 6 rebounds and 2 blocks at halftime .

Additionally, Reese recorded her 30th double-double of the season with Thursday's performance. She had already set the record for double-doubles in a single season when she got her 29th in an 89-81 win over the Minnesota Lynx on Aug. 30.

Reese also tallied a 30-point, 10-rebound game in the fewest minutes during a game in WNBA history , playing only 25.

In her third WNBA season, her first with Atlanta, Reese is averaging a career-best 16.5 points per game, in addition to 12.4 rebounds. And she's putting up those numbers for a championship contender. At 28-14, the Dream are tied for the No. 3 seed in the WNBA standings .

Rhyne Howard having career-best season in scoring and shooting

Howard came into Thursday's game tied with Ionescu, but missed her first eight shots from behind the arc before finally sinking a 3 for the record. She finished with 10 points, 6 rebounds, 8 assists and 4 steals.

For the season, Howard is shooting 36% (129-for-358) from long range, the best percentage of her career while also taking her highest volume of 3-point shots. The five-year veteran is the Dream's second-leading scorer this season behind Allisha Gray , averaging 18.1 points per game while shooting 41% from the floor, both career-best marks.

The Dream close out their home schedule by hosting the Chicago Sky (15-26). Atlanta then ends the regular season with two games at the New York Liberty (24-16).

articles.title: Stephen Curry’s $137 million Warriors news gets a positive update ahead of two-year max extension with the franchise
articles.summary: NBA News: Stephen Curry's $137 million extension decision with the Golden State Warriors is edging toward a resolution, and everything coming out of the Bay Are.
articles.body: Stephen Curry's $137 million extension decision with the Golden State Warriors is edging toward a resolution, and everything coming out of the Bay Area points somewhere favorable for the franchise. Golden State's front office handed the two-time MVP a menu of contract paths back in August, then stepped away and let him work through it without applying pressure. That patience looks like it is paying off, since Curry has quietly made clear he wants to finish his career right where he started.Warriors insider Anthony Slater expects Curry to settle on an answer within the next ten days, well before media day on September 28 in San Francisco. Whichever version of the deal he picks, the guard many consider the engine of this whole era looks locked in on staying.Stephen Curry reaffirms Warriors' commitment amid contract talksStephen Curry became extension eligible on August 29, putting a two-year, $136.7 million offer on the table that the front office left entirely in his hands. Slater said Golden State's decision-makers refused to negotiate on dollar figures and instead gave Curry several paths to pick from, ranging from the outright max to a lighter deal that would open up cap room for next summer. He compared it to a waiter setting down a menu and walking away for a few weeks, adding that Stephen Curry will come back to them and tell them what he wants.Curry has been just as direct in his own words. Asked if a free agency tour similar to the one LeBron James took this past offseason held any appeal, the four time champion shut it down without hesitation, saying he's always stated that he wanna be a lifer with Golden State. That line alone strips away most of the uncertainty hanging over the situation. The $137 million star is not shopping himself around. He is deciding how, not whether, he stays.Warriors' cap space could reshape the roster around CurryWhatever number Curry eventually signs at will shape how much room Golden State has to work with. If he takes something closer to $40 million a year instead of the full max, the Warriors could unlock somewhere between $64 and $70 million in space once Jimmy Butler's and Draymond Green's contracts come off the books. Even if Curry takes the full max, Golden State should still carry roughly $40 million in flexibility heading into next offseason.Golden State heads to Hawaii for training camp already knowing where this is headed, even if the paperwork isn't signed yet.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Una Final Four para empezar
articles.standfirst: El Real Madrid inicia su nuevo proyecto en Abu Dabi
articles.summary: El Real Madrid inicia su nuevo proyecto en Abu Dabi
articles.body: Oficialmente, el Real Madrid inicia su nuevo proyecto en Abu Dabi. Allí se pone en juego el primer título de la temporada, la SuperCup de la Euroliga que estrena competición. Su campeón se conocerá incluso antes del de la Supercopa Endesa. Pero para los blancos el torneo tiene un doble interés además de tratar de levantar el primer trofeo de la temporada. Es posible que los detractores de esta nueva competición argumenten aquello de 'como había pocos partidos, metemos más'. Son dos partidos más para los equipos que compiten pero probablemente todos ellos contaran con esos duelos a la hora de conformar sus respectivas pretemporadas. Eso sí, el cartel es tan goloso que es casi imposible dar la espalda a un torneo en el que miden fuerzas cuatro de los equipos más potentes de la Euroliga. Para este torneo de estreno, la Euroliga cuenta con el vigente campeón, el Olympiacos, el finalista, el Real Madrid, el campeón del año anterior, el Fenerbahce, y el equipo anfitrión, el Dubai Basketball. Puestos a pronosticar, es muy posible que tres de los cuatro equipos de la SuperCup estén en mayo en el mismo escenario, el Etihad Arena, jugando la Final Four de la Euroliga. Eso si todo lo deportivo y lo geopolítico transcurre con normalidad. El formato de la competición enfrentará en la primera semifinal (viernes, 16.00, hora peninsular) al Olympiacos con el Fenerbahce y en la segunda (viernes, 19.00 hora peninsular), al Real Madrid con el Dubai. El sábado serán los partidos por el tercer puesto (16.00) y la gran final (19.00). Para el Madrid es un excelente torneo de preparación. Es verdad que el viaje es largo, además a una zona complicada en lo político, pero es que el Madrid arranca la liga regular de la Euroliga a 139 kilómetros de distancia, apenas a una hora y media por carretera, en Dubái. Así que los blancos se medirán este viernes al rival con el que empezarán la lucha por la duodécima Euroliga. El plan del Madrid es que, tras la SuperCup, toda la expedición permanezca en Abu Dabi entrenando hasta el miércoles que es cuando se trasladarán a Dubái para jugar el jueves (18.00). La de Abu Dabi, pues, es la primera Final Four del Madrid. Cuatro equipos candidatos durante la temporada midiendo sus fuerzas. Eso sí, con la temporada recién arrancada. Lo que el equipo de Pedro Martínez desea es realizar este mismo viaje en mayo y ya con el título más importante de la temporada en juego. El Madrid afronta la SuperCup en pleno proceso de encaje de piezas. Durante la pretemporada han sufrido una profunda reestructuración de la plantilla con muchas piezas nuevas, algunas como el caso de Nick Smith jr., que está en la expedición blanca a Abu Dabi, recién llegadas. Será una gran oportunidad para Pedro Martínez, nuevo en el cargo, para ver si han sido absorbidos los conceptos de la pretemporada y si los nuevos van adquiriendo automatismos, ya ante un rival de mucha envergadura y sobre todo con la sensación de un título oficial en juego, por mucho que sea la SuperCup. Además de Pedro Martínez, hasta siete caras nuevas presenta el Madrid esta temporada: Max Shulga, Luwawu-Cabarrot, Mika Jantunen (con algún problemilla para pasar por inmigración en Abu Dabi), Jaime Pradilla, Damian Jones, Olivier Sarr y el recién llegado Smith. De algunos de ellos se espera un impacto inmediato por su conocimiento del baloncesto en España y del propio equipo, como Luwawu-Cabarrot o Pradilla. De otros se confía en una rápida adaptación al juego que quiere Pedro Martínez y del que ya se han podido ver algunos trazos durante la temporada. Si al técnico catalán le encajan bien las piezas, da la impresión de que los aficionados del Madrid se van a divertir mucho esta temporada. Y no sólo el Madrid presentará en sociedad a sus novedades, también lo harán el Olympiacos, que potenció su plantilla campeona con Jean Montero, que llegó más tarde por problemas con su visado, Codi Miller-McIntyre, el Fenerbahce, también con muchas caras nuevas como Ignas Sargiunas, Sertac Sanli, Shavon Shields, Trent Forrest, Braxton Key, Shane Larkin, Marcus Bingham Jr., Will Clyburn, y el Dubai, que ha tirado de talonario para formar una plantilla temible con los fichajes de Xavi Pascual, Tornike Shengelia, Mamadi Diakite, Jaron Blossomgame, Elie Okobo y Thomas Walkup. El Olympiacos, demostrando su fortaleza, llega a la SuperCup sin haber perdido en pretemporada, 5-0, ganando al Promitheas, Fenerbahce, Estrella Roja, dos veces, y Maccabi. El Madrid cayó en su estreno con el Río Breogán y luego ganó al Baskonia, La Laguna y Unicaja. El Fenerbahce perdió con el Glint Korfez Basket y con el Olympiacos y ganó al Tofas, al Armani Milán y al Balkan Botevgrad. El Dubai por su parte repartió triunfos y derrotas (2-2). Ganó al Besiktas y al Anadolu Efes y perdió con el Turk y con el Bahcesehir.

articles.title: ‘Don’t entertain that’-Royce White fires back at Montrezl Harrell over ‘corny’ WNBA insult
articles.summary: Royce White has hit back at Montrezl Harrell after the former NBA Sixth Man of the Year criticised White’s recent WNBA campaign and described the publicity s...
articles.body:
Royce White has hit back at Montrezl Harrell after the former NBA Sixth Man of the Year criticised White's recent WNBA campaign and described the publicity stunts as "corny and lame".

White and former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom have both sought entry into the WNBA Draft as part of a campaign centred on transgender participation in women's sports. White later attended an Indiana Fever game wearing a blonde wig after his draft bid was rejected.

The move has drawn attention around the league, with Harrell now offering his own response during an interview with Scoop B.

Royce White responds after Montrezl Harrell calls WNBA stunts "corny"

Harrell, who described himself as an avid WNBA fan, said he did not support White and Freedom using the league to make their political point.

"I don't entertain that, to be honest with you. That stuff is corny and lame. I'm an actual WNBA fan… For guys like that to use their platform to disrespect it, that's corny. I'm not a fan of it at all. You don't gain any cool points off of it. You're two grown men running into arenas and public spaces making a mockery of yourselves. Who is that helping?"

Harrell also argued that those seeking to discuss the issue should do so directly rather than through public stunts.

"I know what you're trying to say about men not playing with women, but just use your words as a grown man. Don't try to berate women… I'm not a fan of it and wish it was something they wouldn't do, because it's not highlighting the message they claim to have about protecting women's sports."

White subsequently responded to Harrell in a text message, using highly inflammatory language while questioning why Harrell had not previously spoken publicly about the issue.

"This is how b****** talk… 'It's not what you're saying, it's how you're saying it.' Find a more 'politically correct' way to tell me the truth. I'm fresh out of nice ways to tell d*** ***** common sense. It's funny saying 'use your words' like this hasn't already been a discussion for a while. Why hasn't he ever spoken on it or 'used his words' since he gets it?"

White has also indicated that his legal team is preparing for a potential legal battle concerning the WNBA's gender eligibility guidelines.

The exchange adds another layer to an ongoing debate that has already drawn responses from

WNBA players and officials, with White continuing to pursue his challenge to the league.

articles.title: How a potential $1500 risk has improved Caitlin Clark’s relationship with WNBA refs
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark has finally found a way to improve her relationship with WNBA referees. Despite being one of the faces of the WNBA, Indiana Fever star Caitlin...
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark has finally found a way to improve her relationship with WNBA referees.

Despite being one of the faces of the WNBA, Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark has had way too many altercations with referees.

Why? Well, because the Fever star is always on the hunt to get foul calls, but fighting with them doesn't help her much.

In fact, Clark already has seven technical fouls to her name this season. Ironically, this is what has helped Clark improve her relationship with WNBA referees.

Caitlin Clark gets honest being on the verge of receiving eighth technical foul

With just four regular-season games left, if Clark gets another technical foul she will receive an automatic one-game suspension combined with a $1500 fine from the WNBA.

However, this exact reason is why Clark has learned how to communicate her points better to the refs.

"I mean, I think it's certainly been like a conscious effort about it, and I think it's helped me play better basketball.

"It's just like focus on what I need to focus on, you know, and let the last play go. Like, you can't go back in time and change things," Clark said.

She added, "I feel like the refs might also know I have seven technical fouls, so I always try to warn them, like, I'm working with you, I'm working with you, like, let's have a conversation.

"I think it's made my conversations with them more positive and more conversational in both ways for them and for me."

Clark also pointed out that with just four games left in the regular season, her foul count will reset before the playoffs.

This could mean Clark goes off on the refs during the final game of the season. Of course, it needs to be a valid reason; otherwise, fans may turn on Clark.

articles.title: ‘She Is Irrelevant,’ ‘Pathetic’ — Basketball World Fumes As Ex-ESPN Host Accuses WNBA of ‘Coddling’ Caitlin Clark, Ignoring ‘Extremely Nasty’ Fanbase
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark’s arrival in the WNBA helped push women’s basketball to a new level of mainstream attention. From record-setting television audiences to packed...
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark's arrival in the WNBA helped push women's basketball to a new level of mainstream attention. From record-setting television audiences to packed arenas, the "Caitlin Clark effect" quickly became one of the biggest storylines surrounding the league.

But with that spotlight also came intense criticism of Clark and, increasingly, the fanbase surrounding her. Now, a former ESPN host has added another chapter to that debate.

Cari Champion's Fiery Comments on Caitlin Clark and Her Fanbase Draw Backlash

On Wednesday, former ESPN host Cari Champion appeared on political commentator Bakari Sellers' podcast, "The Bakari Sellers Show," where she didn't hold back.

Champion argued that Clark's fanbase is overly "entitled" and unable to handle even mild criticism of its favorite player, suggesting that any pushback toward Clark is met with disproportionate outrage online.

"The WNBA is trying to balance this entitled fanbase. … I say they are entitled because they get so upset when you say anything about Caitlin, when you say she doesn't play defense, when you say that she needs to be better on the court in terms of her leadership," Champion said .

"… And by the way, her attention is extreme either way. Either extreme pro or extremely not so, it's extreme. No matter how you talk about her, it's going to be extreme."

She didn't stop there but instead urged the WNBA to take a closer look at Clark's supporters.

"If the W really wants to be taken seriously, they cannot be coddled. And I'm talking about all players. And I think that they're mishandling Caitlin in a time that is so polarizing," Champion continued.

"You have a league of women, 70% Black women, and you are putting your supernova — and that's not my name for her. That is what the numbers are saying, that is what the dollars are saying, that is what her impact is saying — and you're coddling her, and you're ignoring this extremely nasty base."

Champion's comments quickly spread across social media, with clips from the podcast triggering a wave of responses from the basketball world.

One influencer stated that they are tired of certain media personalities repeatedly minimizing Clark's impact while creating what they believe are misleading narratives about her.

"It's nasty, and it's toxic, and it's all these things pertaining to Caitlin Clark and her fan base, but these other players have the exact same type of fan base doing the exact same thing. Even worse, she's quiet; she ignores it; they don't see it. … This lady is pathetic; don't even give her an ounce of your attention after this!!!" the influencer wrote .

Another X user flatly stated they were done being provoked into caring about inflammatory commentary.

"I am genuinely done being rage-baited into giving a [expletive] about opinions from people like Cari Champion. She is irrelevant to the league and its future; she's trying to desperately hold onto the Caitlin hate train so she can get some clout out of it," the user said .

"They really hate that they can't control the narrative anymore. This is so hilarious, it's time to break glass on Bakari Sellers. OMG," another reacted .

Team USA recently defeated France 97-79 in Berlin to win its fifth consecutive FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup title. Clark contributed 12 points in the final as the Americans overcame an early 14-point deficit.

One user pointed out that Clark's global popularity was visible in Germany throughout the tournament, with fans from European countries showing support.

"Significant number in the crowd with Caitlin jerseys on, and not just at the USA games. She was one of the players who received the biggest reception outside of the Germany team. (I've got the videos to prove it). This was in Europe!" the user wrote .

While most of the reactions focused on Champion's comments about Clark and her fanbase, one user took a different approach, bringing up her connection to ESPN's Stephen A. Smith.

"Stephen A. Smith breathed new life into this woman's career, and this is how she's going about utilizing her last 15 minutes of fame. Wild," the user said .

As the dust settles, it is clear that whether critics like it or not, Clark's shadow and her fanbase's passion continue to loom large over the sport.

articles.title: Mirotic: "Sigo con hambre de ganar"
articles.standfirst: El ala-pívot de 35 años, presentado como nuevo jugador del Valencia Basket
articles.summary: El ala-pívot de 35 años, presentado como nuevo jugador del Valencia Basket
articles.body: El ala-pívot Nikola Mirotic aseguró este viernes, en su presentación como nuevo jugador del Valencia Basket, que, pese a su ya larga carrera, mantiene la ambición por volver a ganar títulos y dijo que espera hacerlo con su nuevo equipo como lo ha hecho con los anteriores. "Sigo con hambre de ganar. En todos los sitios en los que he estado he ganado títulos y espero seguir haciendo esto aquí", señaló el jugador nacido en Montenegro y con nacionalidad española. "Estoy con ganas de poder ayudar al equipo a seguir construyendo algo especial y de ayudar a la gente joven. También de poder ayudar al 'staff' con mi experiencia. Me siento capacitado de hacerlo y vine directo sin dormir porque tenía ganas de no perderme días porque estaba cerca la Supercopa y quería ser parte del equipo", añadió Mirotic, que admitió que su presencia en el torneo no es segura por cuestiones burocráticas. El ex del Real Madrid y del Barcelona dijo que para él "es un orgullo" jugar en el Valencia Basket y más en una temporada como la de su cuadragésimo aniversario. "Tiene mucha historia por detrás y esto es símbolo de que habrá mucha historia por delante. Son 40 años construyendo algo especial y formar parte de este proyecto es algo especial", apuntó. Además, dijo que quiere ayudar a dar continuidad a los éxitos de la pasada campaña, en la que el equipo llegó a la Final a Cuatro de la Euroliga y conquistó la Supercopa y la Liga Endesa. "Este equipo va a seguir haciendo lo mismo o intentando ser mejor. Ir de menos a más, ir construyendo a un club que ya está en un nivel muy alto y que la gente piense de Valencia como un club que va a competir por todos los títulos. El Valencia una vez más va a estar lo más arriba posible", auguró. "No vamos a hablar de presión porque siempre se espera mucho y estoy acostumbrado a tener esa presión. Por mí no hay problema. Espero que podamos dar lo que la afición pide, esfuerzo y compromiso, y que podamos hacer disfrutar a toda la ciudad", añadió. Mirotic dijo que la pasada campaña en el Mónaco no fue "fácil" y agradeció al Valencia haber confiado en él. "Está en mis manos devolver ese compromiso y dar lo mejor que pueda para dar las gracias por la confianza", dijo. El ala-pívot dijo que cuando surgió el interés del Valencia Basket este verano para él fue un "objetivo claro" poder cerrar la operación. "Hablé con mi agente y le dije si había alguna opción que íbamos para adelante", explicó. "Se dio todo muy rápido. Hay detalles en los que yo no me meto. Llevábamos tiempo hablando y lo que sí sé es que cuando todo estuvo a punto de cerrarse estaba con mi familia y con mis hijos a las 5 de la tarde en la piscina. Me dijo mi agente 'si quieres, lo cerramos ya' y esa noche estaba ya volando", recordó. Mirotic dijo que el Valencia "es un club con trayectoria" y que está "en una gran dirección". "Ha ganado títulos, ha jugado la Final Four, es un proyecto muy bonito, en una gran ciudad y con gran afición. He escuchado muchas cosas positivas y para poder unirme a este proyecto todo cuadraba", analizó. Por su parte, el director de relaciones institucionales del Valencia Basket, Víctor Luengo, dijo que la trayectoria y palmarés de Mirotic "hablan por sí solos" y destacó que "ha aceptado el reto de subirse a un tren en marcha y ya ha demostrado su predisposición para ponerse al ritmo del equipo que lleva un mes entrenándose". "Se vino casi sin dormir para entrenar cuanto antes. Ha venido para sumar y no necesitará mucho tiempo para ser un jugador importante", auguró.

articles.title: Top 2027 NBA Draft Prospects To Know at Every Position
articles.summary: NBA teams scouting prospects likely to separate them by archetype to make it easier to identify their projected roles.
articles.body:
NBA teams scouting prospects likely to separate them by archetype to make it easier to identify their projected roles.

The position chart keeps on evolving. While there are still guards, forwards and centers, it's worth breaking them down even further.

Primary ball-handling guards play and defend only one position: The traditional point guard spot.

Combo guards can be interchangeable in the backcourt.

Off-ball guards/wings will play off the ball, aren't used as much to create and will usually defend 1s, 2s and sometimes 3s.

Initiator wings are forwards size-wise who often handle the ball and create.

Frontcourt off-ball wings will likely play the 3 and score, but offense won't run through their ball-handling.

Combo forwards have the size to play the 4 with enough perimeter skill and mobility to play the 3.

Power forwards have inside-out skill, but aren't big or defensive-minded enough to play center. They aren't shifty or quick enough on the perimeter to be a wing.

Interchangeable bigs have the size to play center with enough perimeter skill to play the 4.

Centers lack perimeter skill/movement and play one position using their size around the basket at both ends.

The conversation around Sadler changed after his 29-point game at the Nike Hoop Summit. For a 6'0" guard, he still has to show scouts that his shooting is on track to be a surefire plus, but Sadler's ability to create advantages, get to spots, set the table and finish with improvisation/craft looks special.

Unless we see a surplus of surprise breakouts, Tanner should have a clearer path to the first round in 2027. The only realistic way to ease concerns over his 167-pound frame will be to raise his shotmaking to nuclear levels, considering scouts still hesitated while he made 1.7 threes, excelled as a finisher, produced a strong assist-to-turnover ratio and put up outlier small-guard numbers like 18 dunks and 12 blocks. Interest in Tanner will ultimately revolve around his ability to create advantages, rim pressure and defensive breakdowns.

Powerful, explosive and shifty, James creates rim pressure and highlights around the rim. He's also a true playmaker who'll use his gravity and vision to set up teammates. He'll draw more NBA attention if he's able to take a step forward with his shotmaking, particularly with his pull-up and floater. He did make 45.8 percent of his catch-and-shoot attempts.

Rippey may become more of a 2028 draft prospect with Caleb Foster, Cayden Boozer and John Blackwell ahead of him on Duke's depth chart. His explosiveness, advantage creation and playmaking are still exciting long-term, while his energy and defense should also help him earn freshman minutes. How convincing his shooting and overall efficiency look this season will likely determine whether NBA teams are willing to buy right away in 2027.

Fears just had one of the most productive playmaking seasons on record, joining four others (including Ja Morant and Kris Dunn) to register a 50.0 assist percentage. There is still hesitation from scouts around the combination of limited size, weak finishing and low-volume three-point shooting. That said, he has become so advanced running offense, making decisions and creating for others while still posing a threat with his catch-and-shoot stroke and pull-up.

Arkansas' offense will run through Smith's ability to pressure defenses with transition speed and explosive rim pressure. Skeptics will question his playmaking for a lead guard and his size for a 2, but he has the athletic traits, shotmaking potential and defensive intensity that can help evaluators picture outlier outcomes.

No freshman possesses more shotmaking skill or scoring instincts than Crowe. His self-creation, shooting versatility and range/confidence can lead to the type of instant offense that can execute against any defense. Scouts will just want to see some degree of competent playmaking (and enough efficiency) for a 6'4", 190-pound guard who isn't going to generate easy rim pressure.

Mingo has size for both backcourt spots, with a handle and shiftiness to create advantages off the dribble. He's shown encouraging flashes of shotmaking and playmaking, while his 6'5" frame and length give him the tools to defend multiple positions. His NBA and draft ceilings will hinge largely on becoming a more consistent three-point shooter and proving he can stay healthy.

Coleman is a versatile guard who should give Illinois another ball-handler with enough size and shotmaking to play off the ball. His role will likely center on providing secondary creation, perimeter scoring and athletic playmaking.

Arenas shot just 34.1 percent in 14 games last year, but offseason injuries and a late start deserve blame. His natural talent and skill for creation and shotmaking are evident. At 6'6" with a dangerous handle, three-level scoring ability and playmaking potential, he'll jump right back into the first-round discussion if he's able to execute with far more efficiency.

At 6'5", Holt is more of an undersized wing who compensates for limited height and creation with physicality, shotmaking, off-ball scoring versatility and defense. It's difficult to label Holt with a specific position, given the various roles and spots on the floor he plays and the fact that his game keeps evolving. With more offense likely to run through Ivan Kharchenkov and Derek Dixon, Holt will likely operate as an off-ball wing who'll provide some secondary playmaking in transition and limited ball-screen situations.

Howard seems more like a 2028 draft prospect with Duke bringing back Caleb Foster, Cayden Boozer and Dame Sarr while adding John Blackwell to the backcourt. He should still draw NBA scouts' attention this year with his solid frame, perimeter creation and confident shotmaking. He'll play mostly off the ball and, presumably, look to improve his off-the-dribble game, three-level scoring and playmaking ability further down the road.

While scouts sound divided on Mullins' NBA ceiling, his positional size, advanced shotmaking and functional athleticism make him an easy fit, high floor and useful archetype for many teams. He should have more opportunities to work in ball screens and experiment in creation situations.

Toure should make his mark with athletic-driven creation and finishing. The burst, power and explosion should translate to rim pressure, easy buckets and defensive activity. He's ultimately become a lottery name to watch by improving his shooting, both off the catch and dribble. The consistency of his shot will likely factor heavily into whether Toure can enter the conversation with the top freshman prospects in the nation.

Adams is a strong, skilled wing whose footwork, pull-up shooting and three-point range should stand out quickly, even if he's reduced to a reserve role. He's not an explosive athlete or dynamic creator, but his feel, physicality and shotmaking should stand out quickly.

Landing Spots for Top 5 Unsigned NBA Free Agents 🏀

Knicks walk back ticket pricing increase

Scouts have been penciling Stokes atop the 2027 draft board for years. While it's difficult to give him a specific position, he profiles as a 6'8", 230-pound forward who'll take on ball-handler and creation duties. His three-level scoring and playmaking flashes are wing-like; only he possesses the frame and strength of a 4.

He possesses mismatch tools and skills. Convincing lottery teams that he's the surefire top prospect will mean erasing concerns over his decision-making and scoring efficiency.

Joksimovic has crept into the top-five discussion after MVP showings at Eurocamp and the U18 European Championships. He has the positional size, creativity, shotmaking and some vertical pop at the rim. He just isn't a high-level facilitator, and lingering questions remain about his defensive outlook in the NBA.

Though not an isolation scorer, Kharchenkov should see more on-ball reps given how well he's able to drive, make touch shots and make passing reads. He also brings tone-changing competitiveness at both ends of the floor. Scouts should picture an easy fit at the next level, but Kharchenkov has a real chance to rise up boards if he improves his creation and pull-up game.

Scouts started to gradually pick up on Allen's physical tools, shotmaking and secondary playmaking flashes (3.1 assists), which always create coveted versatility. The microscope on his ball-handling development and shooting consistency will intensify as his usage spikes for Alabama this year.

Vaaks, 6'7", was the only player last year above 6'5" with 90 made threes and an assist percentage of 18.0. He's a dangerous shooter off the catch and dribble, but he also logged 171 pick-and-roll ball-handling possessions at Providence. The athletic and defensive questions are real, but Vaaks is still worth monitoring as a big wing who can initiate offense and launch from everywhere around the perimeter.

Andrews packs physicality at 6'6", 225 pounds, with budding perimeter scoring skills. He's a power wing who could potentially scale up to the 4 in certain matchups. Showing more growth with his three-point range and pull-up game at Arkansas should guarantee NBA interest during his first season.

Branch will look the part with solid NBA wing size and the ability to score from three levels with drives and self-created jumpers. While limited playmakers have less margin for error, Branch still shows the advanced footwork and shotmaking synonymous with high-level scoring prospects.

Landrew is listed at 236 pounds and clearly possesses next-level footwork, finishing craft and shotmaking skill. The eye test suggests a surefire pro wing prospect. He could beat out Jayden Ross for minutes if he's consistent enough with his jumper and defensive reads.

Fogle's size, skill set and advanced stats suggest he is poised to draw NBA attention in a bigger role with strong supporting talent. He was a productive shotmaker from three levels with athletic pop around the basket, strong defensive playmaking rates, an efficient assist-to-turnover ratio and promising glimpses of secondary creation in ball-screen situations.

Oladotun's 6'10" size and smooth perimeter scoring and shooting should pop instantly at Maryland. Scouts will start to take him seriously if he's able to show he can score efficiently in more ways inside the arc, where there may be some concerns about his thin frame and explosion.

Thompson should pop instantly with clean three-point shooting at 6'9", 215 pounds. He's been consistent from deep during his prime high school years. He complements the catch-and-shoot stroke with transition finishing and post scoring. How much he's able to show in between will determine how high he climbs up the boards.

Yimga-Moukouri enters his draft-eligible season with Nanterre 92, where he should see an expanded role after averaging roughly nine points in limited minutes as a 17-year-old and then leading France at the 2026 U18 EuroBasket with 17.3 points and 5.6 rebounds per game. Physically, the 6'8" forward already looks the part physically, with improved spot-up shooting. His next step is developing more creation skills and feel off the dribble—particularly his handle, passing reads and decision-making—which could determine whether he projects primarily as a complementary two-way forward or offers more offensive upside.

Passing on the past two drafts could diminish the allure around Haugh's pro potential, considering he'll turn 24 before the 2027-28 NBA season. His clear NBA fit, plus the likelihood he's the top player for a surefire National Championship contender, should keep plenty of interest alive. Even at his age, there will be teams willing to use a top-20 pick on a 6'9" combo forward who shoots threes, explodes above the rim and brings connective skill/IQ.

At 6'8", 219 pounds, Gaskins looks like a 4 physically, with a promising stroke for pick-and-pop threes and elbow jumpers. He seems to be gradually evolving into a big-wing type who can also attack ball screens and closeouts.

Morillo will generate conversation around his versatility, being a 6'7" wing who operates as a pick-and-roll ball-handler and connective piece. Whether he's able to sell teams on his shooting potential will likely determine whether he's viewed as a real NBA prospect.

Houindo's 6'10" size, athleticism, instincts around the basket and occasional perimeter flashes have earned him a spot on long-term watch lists for years. Last year's MVP showings at ANGT and Basketball Without Borders raised scouts' awareness and the bar for next season, when he'll likely play a bigger role for Cedevita Olimpija's senior team.

Foot surgery has cost Mirkovic important offseason prep time, which clouds his outlook. He's on NBA radars after hitting 57 threes and registering a 16.2 assist percentage and 20.2 defensive rebounding percentage. Those numbers highlight attractive shooting range, handling/passing and instincts at the rim for a 6'9" forward. His defensive outlook has raised concerns. It's now worth questioning his readiness for the season.

Hansberry suddenly checks intriguing boxes after shooting 35.4 percent from three, averaging 2.4 assists and registering strong defensive playmaking rates at Virginia Tech. He has the tools and rebounding motor of an NBA 4, plus a promising catch-and-shoot stroke and a strong passing IQ.

A torn ACL threw a wrench into Toppin's 2026 draft stock. NBA teams have always wanted to see a more reliable three-point shot, but his outstanding paint production suggests that his interior scoring instincts, short-range touch and rebounding can translate.

Folgueiras's shooting, passing and finishing could receive more attention under the spotlight at Louisville. A 6'9" forward who shot 71.4 percent at the rim at Iowa, has 101 threes in 104 career games and posted a 20.0 percentage in consecutive years, Folgueiras could rise above the radar on a high-profile team this season.

Muurinen has stood out for years with his explosive finishes and perimeter shotmaking for a 7-footer. His talent is obvious. His skill set makes him a surefire fit and valued archetype. Erasing concerns about his decision-making and maturity will be the keys to his draft stock.

Williams' size, movement and shooting flashes are the draws. He'll operate this year as a play-finisher who covers ground defensively and occasionally makes shots from outside the paint. He just may be too raw to play a major offensive role this season for a rotation that has Patrick Ngongba II and potential No. 1 overall 2028 pick Joakim Boumtje Boumtje.

Winter plays the 5 at 7'0", but his shooting and fluidity in attacking closeouts could be useful at the 4 for a big who isn't a huge plus in rim protection. Winter is well-rounded and polished offensively as a post scorer and pick-and-roll/pop big who rebounds and finishes extremely well.

Condon should be able to make his way back into the first-round conversation with signs of improved shooting. He's still currently an attractive prospect at 6'11" with play-finishing bounce and a 20.0 assist percentage, but a more proven three-point shot will change the level of interest in Condon.

Diop is still more of a 5-man finisher and shot-blocker at 7'1", but he clearly shows confidence around the perimeter, both taking threes and putting the ball down. He'll generate real NBA interest at Gonzaga if he looks more polished this year away from the basket.

NBA teams will ignore Krivas' counting stats and instead focus on analytics, tape and measurements that point to an NBA defensive anchor. At 7'2", 260 pounds, he's a massive paint presence in rim protection, as well as a useful low-post scorer, offensive rebounder and roll man with floater touch.

Durability will be a major talking point with Ngongba, who missed Duke games with foot soreness and sat out his entire senior year of high school. When healthy, he's been an effective rim protector, play-finisher and post player with some unique passing IQ and flashes of shooting potential. NBA teams tend to show love for centers who are smart/quick processors.

It felt like Suigo had a chance to go first round last year, especially after he measured nearly 7'3" barefoot at the NBA Combine. He's a massive presence around the basket, with fluid finishing and overwhelming tools for offensive rebounding and shot-blocking. After hitting 24 threes, building on those flashes of shooting touch at Villanova could really help raise the excitement around his NBA outlook.

On a per-minute basis, no other player combined for better shot-blocking and offensive rebounding rates than Hines. In a bigger role and under a brighter spotlight at Connecticut, his impact this year should be magnified. Despite lacking any real creation or scoring skills beyond finishing and post-ups, his paint presence and defense look strong enough for scouts to look past the limited offensive versatility.

Moreno was close to entering last year's draft, but returning to a role with more touches and offensive responsibility made sense. NBA teams admire his instincts, which show in his passes and defensive reads. He'll enter the 2027 first-round discussion as a bigger post threat and a dangerous play-finisher.

articles.title: 5 NBA Stars Who Could Dominate Trade Rumors This Season
articles.summary: The trade market scattered stars all around the NBA this offseason.
articles.body:
The trade market scattered stars all around the NBA this offseason.

The upcoming 2026-27 campaign just might do the same.

Conditions remain perfect for some landscape-shifting deals. Not every trade candidate found a new hoops home, and not every talent-pursuing team closed a fortune-changing transaction.

So, what's coming next? Well, it's funny (and fortunate) you should ask, since we're here to examine five stars who could keep the rumor mill moving for reasons we'll detail as we discuss each one.

The Wizards only acquired Davis in February, and he hasn't suited up for them yet, so this would be a pretty speedy divorce. Then again, there were whispers about a possible split as soon as this summer, and the same particulars that spawned them remain in place.

The timelines are completely disconnected. Davis is 33 years old and very much in win-immediately mode, while the still-rebuilding Wizards are coming off three consecutive seasons with 64-plus losses. Washington could be markedly improved this season and still nowhere near the title chase; that just isn't the kind of carrot on the stake Davis wants to chase at this stage of his career.

His unsettled future plays a big part in potential trade talks, too. His contract features a $62.8 million player option for next season and nothing beyond that. Washington could try to extend him, obviously, but it could be pretty costly, as Yahoo Sports' Kevin O'Connor relayed there were "rumblings [that Davis is] demanding that full max from Washington but would sign for less if traded to a contender."

Nothing feels particularly sturdy, then, when it comes to the foundation of this relationship. Other clubs can surely sense that, too, and might pester the Wizards with trade inquiries, especially if Davis looks healthy.

If he is up to form, he is worth a small fortune to the right suitor—even with tricky extension negotiations ahead. The last time he held up for 60-plus games (2023-24), he was an All-Star, an All-Defensive first-teamer and an All-NBA second-teamer that season.

His availability and contract concerns are real, but so is the fact that his 26.68 career player efficiency rating is fifth-highest in NBA history.

When the Clippers acquired Garland at this past trade deadline, they may have viewed him as a building block for their backcourt. But plenty has changed since, and it's easy to imagine that (or at least wonder if) plans with Garland have changed, too.

For starters, L.A.'s fortune at the draft lottery netted the team another young, offense-first guard in Keaton Wagler. While there's enough off-ball utility for the pair to function on offense, the defensive challenge could torpedo all of that production—and then some.

More importantly, though, the Clippers learned their punishments from the salary-cap circumvention investigation, and they were severe enough to impact whatever plans this group had of growing something organically. L.A. was stripped of five first-round picks, putting its future into an impossible predicament.

The Clippers have to be searching for ways to dig out of this draft deficit, and a trade involving Garland almost assuredly promises the most relief. The right offensively limited suitor could potentially fork over multiple first-round picks to land the 26-year-old, two-time All-Star.

He is shifty with his handle, deep with his shooting range and reliable with his playmaking. He has flirted with 50/40/90 efficiency before, routinely has a sizable gap between his assists and turnovers and seems capable of more than the 20-ish points he has averaged in multi-creator offenses.

There might be a movie executive or three hoping Herro's return to his home state of Wisconsin plays out in superheroic style befitting of his Boy Wonder nickname. A franchise gutted by the forced exit of its best player in history gets miraculously saved by, essentially, a hometown hero? Yeah, the script sort of writes itself.

Unfortunately, there a number of different ways in which that scenario gets reality-checked toward something a lot less exciting. Even Herro acknowledged this uncertainty when telling The Athletic's Eric Nehm that his homecoming might last "for two months, two years, whatever it is."

While Herro should clear the two month threshold soon, he is hardly guaranteed a full season-plus stay in the Badger State. The Bucks, for one, might be too far removed from any kind of competitive window to justify hanging onto a 26-year-old All-Star over flipping him for, perhaps, a midsize pile of long-term assets.

Or maybe the Bucks just aren't inclined to commit anything beyond Herro's current contract, which expires at season's end, to such a one-way contributor. Especially when his offensive value could be muted by the backcourt presences of Ryan Rollins, Kevin Porter Jr. and lottery pick Brayden Burries (not to mention playmaking forwards Jaime Jaquez Jr. and Nate Ament).

Any number of factors could push Herro into the rumor mill, and he could generate a good amount of buzz upon his arrival. His defensive flaws are real, but his offensive punch is powerful. He is one of only six players to average at least 20 points, four assists and 2.5 three-pointers in each of the past five seasons.

The Mavericks keep insisting they have geniune interest in seeing how Irving operates alongside reigning Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg. Folks just aren't buying it, or at least not buying the concept of that interest holding greater appeal than the chunk of assets Irving could return in a deal.

As NBA insider Marc Stein put it, rival teams "continue to wonder aloud about how firmly Dallas will stick to that stance once the season begins and the next in-season trade deadline on Feb. 11 gradually approaches."

Even if that skepticism features a bit of optimism, it's still warranted. Irving and Flagg just might harmonize on the hardwood, but there's no way to unite the timelines attached to the 34-year-old Irving and the 19-year-old Flagg. And since the franchise's focus should be absolutely affixed to Flagg's future, Irving's present value to the organization may only extend to wherever the trade market sets it.

The good news is that Irving should have at least a decent market. He has his warts—a spotty injury history, a few bridge-burning breaks from his ex-employers and an unsettled financial future —but his resume is rich enough to outshine them all, especially for suitors shopping for scoring, shotmaking and all kinds of creativity.

The last time Irving played—he missed all of last season while recovering from a torn ACL—he earned All-Star honors while averaging 24.7 points on 47.3/40.1/91.6 shooting with 4.6 assists against 2.2 turnovers. And he did so while navigating around the wrecking ball that was the disastrous Luka Dončić deal.

Of all the myriad ways in which the Bulls could've used their cap space this summer, investing a big chunk of it into Powell ahead of his age-33 season didn't appear on most Bingo cards. Yet, they both decided that was the best course of action—perhaps a reflection of (and reaction to) what was and wasn't available to them.

Chicago following Powell's $21.5 million salary for this season with a $22.8 million team option for 2027-28 seems an admission from both parties that this relationship could (and arguably should) be short-lived. The Bulls are still sketching out their rebuilding blueprint and have, as Powell told FadeawayWorld's Mark Medina "the potential to be really good" but also "the potential to be really bad."

Oddsmakers think it'll be the latter , which could put a ticking clock on Powell, who had an All-Star case in 2024-25 and then an All-Star selection this past season.

As an efficient support scorer (21.8 points on 47.7/40/81.6 shooting over this stretch) with a fiery three-ball, loads of playoff experience and some self-creation chops, he'd be a real get for a win-now shopper needing an offensive lift. Even as a partial-season rental, he'd bring something of value to the Bulls.

A one-piece-away near-contender could legitimately view Powell as the final addition that pushes it over the proverbial hump. Chicago just happens to need something completely different than he can offer, though it will surely appreciate any veteran wisdom he can share with this young locker room and whatever it is he brings back in a midseason trade.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham says what other gaslighting female athletes won't about the naked Sydney Sweeney ad
articles.summary: Sophie Cunningham defended Sydney Sweeney's Novig gambling ad on her "No Hesitation" podcast, calling the backlash from women athletes overblown.
articles.body: After a full week of women athletes fuming at Sydney Sweeney for, apparently, setting women's sports back decades with her naked gambling ad, Sophie Cunningham has set the record straight. And, to the surprise of approximately nobody, the WNBA's most sane player offered up the most sane take of this entire, silly ordeal. "Why are girls mad?" Cunningham asked on her newly revamped, "No Hesitation" podcast. "That is literally what she does. Why is anyone mad? It is a gambling ad: men, sports, naked women. Of course, that’s going to draw attention. "Do I agree with it? Morally, I think it’s kind of weird, but each to their own. Go do your thing, sis." SYDNEY SWEENEY FIRES BACK AT TROLLS AFTER FACING CRITICISM ONLINE FOR PROVOCATIVE SPORTS AD Sophie Cunningham is back at it Shockingly, it's another home run for Sophie Cunningham. She just doesn't miss. What a run! Look, Cunningham's right. This is what Sweeney does. She likes to take her clothes off, if you haven't noticed. It's sort of her shtick. In fact, the whole ad campaign was her idea, according to Novig CEO Jacob Fortinsky! Sweeney literally came up with the whole thing. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "It really was Sydney who was driving a lot of the visuals and the messaging," he said during a panel earlier this week. "We're hugely supportive of women's sports. I think it's a huge component of our platform. We never intended to portray female sports." Correct. This ad had nothing to do with women's sports. It was about gambling. Aren't they all nowadays? Seems like it. Sweeney was catering to one very specific audience, as her and new podcast partner, Drew Hanlen, pointed out. Drew, who wouldn't stop talking, figured around 75% of sports bettors are men. SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM ADDRESSES PERCEPTION THAT SHE IS THE 'SEX SYMBOL' OF THE WNBA I think that's way off. I'd put it closer to 90%. Maybe 95%. Regardless, that's who the ad was for — and it worked! "I can understand when you first see that ad that like it could kind of deflate women, because it’s like we’ve worked so hard to get a little bit of respect around here," Cunningham continued. "But when you really think about it, it’s like, screw it, let that girl do her thing. This has nothing to do with us. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER "At the end of the day, I’m really loving seeing all these girls who are powerful, strong, showing young girls what it looks like to be an athlete. I don’t think the ad was coming for women in sports." Another win for the WNBA's most sane player.

articles.title: WNBA fans expect Angel Reese punishment after cheeky referee comments
articles.summary: WNBA fans are having a field day after Angel Reese’s praise for FIBA officiating raised eyebrows. Angel Reese has been walking a tightrope with the league of...
articles.body:
WNBA fans are having a field day after Angel Reese 's praise for FIBA officiating raised eyebrows.

Angel Reese has been walking a tightrope with the league office after picking up seven technical fouls this season, coming dangerously close to an automatic suspension before an eighth tech was mercifully rescinded on appeal.

But her constant clashes with whistle-happy refs are just a symptom of a much bigger headache.

The overwhelming feeling across the WNBA right now is pure frustration with the officiating. Players, coaches, and fans are fed up with the lack of consistency, where hard contact is ignored on one end and ticky-tack fouls get called on the other. It's an ongoing debate that keeps boiling over week after week.

Angel Reese praises FIBA officiating after Atlanta Dream win

Angel Reese made WNBA history in Atlanta's blowout win over Connecticut , becoming the fastest player ever to drop 30 points and 10 rebounds in a single game.

However, it wasn't just her performance that drew attention, as Reese praised the officiating of FIBA officials during the World Cup in her Atlanta Dream postgame interview .

She said: "That was my first experience in this environment where we could really play physical. We're so much more free. I love these FIBA refs. They were incredible oh my god, it was crazy."

As you can imagine, supporters went crazy online, suggesting that the WNBA and officials won't take too kindly to her comments.

One fan suggested a backlash from the WNBA referees: "They're gonna give her that 8th T again."

"They're calling a foul on her first thing on Saturday." Another fan said.

Another pointed towards her next game: "She bout to be in foul trouble in the first half of her next game."

"They bout run them pockets." This supporter even suggested a potential fine.

The feeling was mutual: "Oh yeah, they're giving her a tech in the first 5 mins of the game Saturday."

The Atlanta Dream return home to State Farm Arena to host the Chicago Sky on Saturday, September 19 at 7:00 PM ET.

articles.title: Knicks Insider Warns of Potential 'Hangover,' 3-Point Regression After 2026 NBA Title
articles.summary: The New York Knicks are atop the NBA mountaintop after winning their first championship since 1973, but their repeat efforts could face some serious challenges in 2026-27.
articles.body:
The New York Knicks are atop the NBA mountaintop after winning their first championship since 1973, but their repeat efforts could face some serious challenges in 2026-27.

"A team source took a cautious approach when forecasting for next season, warning about the possibility of a championship hangover and noting that the Knicks' 3-point shooting could regress next spring after they ranked first in the 2026 postseason," ESPN's Ben Golliver reported.

Golliver noted that nine of New York's top 10 members of its playoff rotation are returning with only Mitchell Robinson no longer on the roster. The team didn't waste any time finding a replacement, adding Andre Drummond to slide into Robinson's place on the depth chart.

Knicks walk back ticket pricing increase

Still, the Eastern Conference figures to be more challenging this season with LeBron James and Jaylen Brown joining the Philadelphia 76ers, Giannis Antetokounmpo teaming up with Bam Adebayo on the Miami Heat, Tyrese Haliburton returning from injury for the Indiana Pacers, and Kawhi Leonard joining the Toronto Raptors.

Contenders like the Cleveland Cavaliers, Detroit Pistons and Boston Celtics could also be threats for a Knicks team that finished with the No. 3 seed last season before catching fire from deep during the playoffs and riding Jalen Brunson's star power to a title.

Even the slightest regression from three-point range could make a difference with so many contenders in the East, and that's not even getting into a potential NBA Finals matchup with either the Oklahoma City Thunder or San Antonio Spurs.

While New York defeated the Spurs in five games in last season's Finals, San Antonio was up by double digits in all four of its losses. A more experienced Spurs team could be in a better position to close those games out if there was a rematch.

Yet even if the Knicks don't defend their title with back-to-back championships, Brunson and Co. will still be heroes in New York City. After all, that's what happens when you lead a beloved franchise to its first title in 53 years.

articles.title: Angel Reese makes WNBA history with dominant performance in Dream win
articles.summary: Reese scored 30 points and grabbed 10 boards in 25 minutes against Connecticut.
articles.body:
Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese came back from a gold medal run at the FIBA World Cup and extended her WNBA record Thursday, becoming the first player in league history to post 30 double-doubles in one season.

Reese scored 30 points on 11-of-14 shooting and grabbed 10 rebounds in 25 minutes as the Dream beat the Connecticut Sun 103-59 in College Park, Georgia. It was the first WNBA game after a nearly three-week break for the World Cup.

Angel Reese breaks double-doubles record

IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Reese already owned the single-season record before Thursday. She broke the mark of 28 double-doubles set by Phoenix Mercury star Alyssa Thomas in 2023 when she got her 29th against the Minnesota Lynx on Aug. 30.

The 30-point night fell one point shy of her career high, which came in a 31-point, 14-rebound game against the Phoenix Mercury on Aug. 22. The former LSU star did most of her damage early on Thursday, scoring 19 points before halftime.

On Aug. 24, Reese also grabbed 26 rebounds in a 78-71 win over the Los Angeles Sparks , breaking a single-game record that had stood since 2003. That same night, she passed Las Vegas Aces star A'ja Wilson's 2024 total for the most rebounds in a WNBA season .

Atlanta led 45-35 at halftime, but the Dream broke the game open by outscoring Connecticut 31-11 in the third quarter and 27-13 in the fourth.

Dream guard Rhyne Howard set her own WNBA record with 6:45 left, hitting her 129th 3-pointer of the season to pass Sabrina Ionescu 's 2023 mark of 128. Dream guard Allisha Gray added 10 points and broke her own franchise record for points in a season with 782.

"The second half was much better, much more fluid ," Dream head coach Karl Smesko said, per CBS. "Obviously, Angel had a dominant performance tonight. It was fantastic, and everybody contributed all the way down."

"We had a good, hard talk at halftime," Howard said, per CBS. "We're still fighting for something come playoffs, and so we're making sure that we handle our business and that we don't leave anything up to anybody else."

Reese's big night came one day after four-time WNBA champion Tina Thompson pushed her into the WNBA Most Valuable Player race on the "Cousins" podcast with Hall of Famers Vince Carter and Tracy McGrady.

"I also think that Angel needs to be in that conversation. Like, she went there, and that Atlanta team is revived. They're different," Thompson said.

"What Angel Reese does, it impacts winning," Thompson added.

WNBA analyst Nekias Duncan pushed back on social media , pointing out that Atlanta won 30 games and had the league's second-best net rating in 2025, before Reese arrived from the Chicago Sky .

The Dream (27-14) host the Chicago Sky, Reese's former team, on Saturday night. Atlanta is currently the fourth seed for the WNBA playoffs with three games left.

articles.body:
The Cleveland Cavaliers didn't land LeBron James this offseason, but they are reportedly promoting his high school teammate to general manager.

ESPN's Shams Charania reported Friday the Cavaliers promoted Brandon Weems to be their new GM under team president Koby Altman. Weems has been with Cleveland for a decade and had various scouting and personnel roles prior to becoming the assistant GM in 2022.

Cleveland's GM role was open because Mike Gansey joined the Philadelphia 76ers as their president of basketball operations.

The team also named former NBA guard José Calderón as the assistant general manager:

Philadelphia is also where James ended up this offseason, although ESPN noted his agent, Rich Paul, called Weems "basically LeBron's brother" and suggested his presence with the Cavaliers was a major selling point in their pursuit of the King.

After playing high school basketball with James, Weems played collegiately at Walsh University before joining coaching staffs for Oakland University, Drexel and Kentucky.

Since Weems became the assistant GM in Cleveland in February 2022, the Cavaliers have made the playoffs four consecutive years. Last year was their deepest run during that span, as they advanced to the Eastern Conference Finals before losing to the New York Knicks.

Weems has helped put together a consistent Eastern Conference contender that figures to remain on the short list of teams that can realistically make a run to the Finals in 2026-27.

Donovan Mitchell, James Harden, Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen provide plenty of firepower and were just a step away from the sport's biggest stage last season.

articles.summary: El empresario es experto en banca de inversión y cofundador de CRIS contra el Cáncer
articles.body: El Consejo Superior de Deportes (CSD) autorizó la adquisición del control accionarial del Movistar Estudiantes por parte de Sexto Hombre S.L, el nuevo grupo liderado por la empresario Diego Megía, experto en banca de inversión y cofundador de CRIS contra el Cáncer, según anunció el propio club este viernes. Dicho proyecto contempla un compromiso de inversión de 15 millones de euros destinado al desarrollo del equipo, con especial atención al "crecimiento deportivo, la consolidación de la estructura del Club y el impulso de su proyecto de cantera y formación". Con esta autorización queda completado el proceso iniciado el pasado mes de junio, tras el acuerdo alcanzado con los principales accionistas de Movistar Estudiantes. Sin embargo, el inversor Jaime Siles y el empresario Andrés Puyol, quienes lideraron la oferta alternativa de compra del Estudiantes, denunciaron irregularidades y falta de transparencia en el proceso de cambio de propiedad, al no haber sido compartida con los socios y aficionados, ni trasladada al consejo de administración y a los accionistas. De esta forma, el CSD da luz verde a la operación llevada a cabo por la nueva propiedad, aprobada el pasado junio, manteniéndose las "condiciones acordadas". "Tras la autorización del CSD, Sexto Hombre S.L. extenderá su oferta de adquisición de acciones al resto de accionistas de Movistar Estudiantes, en las mismas condiciones que las acordadas con los accionistas de referencia", informó el club. El primer equipo masculino del Estudiantes disputará la Primera FEB, segunda categoría del baloncesto nacional, mientras que su equipo femenino, disputará una nueva campaña en la Liga Femenina Endesa, primera división femenina en España.

articles.title: Ricky Rubio: "No sentimos presión... la mentalidad es ganar la Supercopa"

articles.summary: El capitán del Joventut, anfitrión del primer torneo oficial del curso, se muestra ambicioso
articles.body: El base del Asisa Joventut Ricky Rubio aseguró este viernes que el conjunto verdinegro no siente "presión" por ser el anfitrión de la Supercopa Endesa, pero sí "la ilusión de hacer un gran papel" en la competición que se disputará este fin de semana en el Palau Olímpic de Badalona. "No sentimos presión, pero sí la ilusión de hacer un gran papel. Tenemos la exigencia que nos ponemos nosotros mismos. La mentalidad es ganar la Supercopa, pero se verá mañana", aseguró el jugador del Masnou en declaraciones a los medios de comunicación en la zona mixta del Olímpic en la previa de la semifinal frente al Kosner Baskonia. Rubio recordó que el curso pasado la Penya fue "muy fuerte" frente a su afición y expresó su deseo de "seguir en la misma línea" como locales. "Jugar en casa siempre tiene este aliciente de ilusión y ganas, de ver a tu gente, y nos motiva", añadió. Sobre el estado de los equipos participantes (Joventut, Kosner Baskonia, Barça y Valencia Basket), el base analizó que "los cuatro han cambiado muchísimo respecto al año pasado" y existen aún "muchos interrogantes de cómo encajará todo". "Ha sido una pretemporada atípica para muchos equipos, han faltado jugadores y no han tenido el rodaje suficiente todavía para definirse como equipo. Es un gran torneo que llega temprano, pero pondrá en jaque todo lo que hemos hecho en la pretemporada. Hay que estar concentrados y saber superar los momentos difíciles. Estamos a dos partidos de un título", expuso Rubio. El internacional español valoró que la Penya llega "un poco mejor que a la Lliga Catalana" tras una semana más de entrenamientos y la incorporación del ala-pívot Eli John Ndiaye, del que elogió su "talento, ambición y ganas". "Tiene la trayectoria suficiente para que pueda llegar lejos. Le falta jugar minutos y aquí encontrará su espacio. Le ayudaremos a descubrir el jugador que puede llegar a ser. Él nos da flexibilidad, puede jugar de 4 y de 5, con un estilo que no teníamos. Nos aporta una herramienta más para ser más peligrosos en todo tipo de escenarios", opinó.

articles.title: Jazz guard Keyonte George reportedly agrees to 5-year, $157.5 million extension
articles.summary: George averaged a career-high 23.6 points and 6.1 assists during the 2025-26 campaign, his third season in the NBA.
articles.body:
With the 2026-27 season fast approaching, Utah Jazz point guard Keyonte George is reportedly finally reaping the benefits of his breakout 2025-26 campaign.

After months of offseason negotiations, George's representation struck a deal with Jazz president of basketball operations Austin Ainge, according to ESPN's Shams Charania , who reported Friday alongside Tim MacMahon that George has agreed to a five-year, $157.5 million rookie-scale extension. It will account for approximately 16% of the franchise's salary cap and doesn't include player or team options, per ESPN's report , and will kick in ahead of the 2027-28 season.

The 22-year-old Baylor product, whom Utah selected 16th overall in the 2023 draft, is coming off the best season of his young NBA career. He averaged a career-high 23.6 points and 6.1 assists for a Jazz franchise that's now primed for a leap toward playoff contention.

Last season, however, Utah posted a 22-60 record. Although the Jazz won five more games than they did the season prior, they were notably fined $500,000 in February for what league officials deemed "conduct detrimental to the league." At the time, Utah was penalized for roster-management decisions that the NBA concluded prioritized draft position over winning, namely the early removal of stars Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. in a pair of games that month.

The Indiana Pacers , accused of violating the NBA's player participation policy, received a similar punishment back then, as the league decried what's colloquially known as "tanking."

Regardless, the Jazz wound up with the No. 2 overall pick in this year's NBA Draft and took Kansas guard Darryn Peterson , who shined in Summer League action after a tantalizing yet turbulent season with the Jayhawks that was marred by cramping issues .

The Jazz will be able to pair Peterson with George in their backcourt this season. Together, they'll help make up a nucleus that also features Markkanen, Jackson and 2025 No. 5 overall pick Ace Bailey , a 20-year-old forward.

George started all 54 games he played in last go-round. He took his game to the next level in Year 3. After back-to-back seasons with a 39.1% field-goal percentage, he bumped that clip to 45.6%. In the process, he shot a personal-best 37.1% from deep.

"We were very happy with the big jump Keyonte made," Ainge said at the end of last season, per The Salt Lake Tribune . "And I think that he even has more to go. I think there are more steps he can take. Obviously, no one peaks at 22, so we think he has even more to grow."

articles.summary: El entrenador azulgrana Aleksander Sekulic reconoce que su presencia les obligará a hacer "ajustes", pero prioriza a su propio equipo
articles.body: El entrenador del Barça, Aleksander Sekulic, aseguró este viernes que el fichaje del ala-pívot Nikola Mirotic por el Valencia Basket, rival de los azulgranas en las semifinales de la Supercopa Endesa, les obligará a hacer "ajustes", aunque el técnico afirmó que se centra más en su propio juego. "Es difícil decir cómo lo van a utilizar. Sabemos lo que Mirotic puede aportar con su experiencia y calidad. Haremos algunos ajustes, pero en este punto del calendario nos centramos más en nuestro juego, en cómo queremos jugar", señaló el preparador esloveno en declaraciones a los medios de comunicación en la pista del Palau Blaugrana. Sekulic comentó que el Barça puede "mejorar en los dos lados de la pista, sobre todo en defensa", si bien señaló que el grupo va "en el buen camino", puesto que "hay una gran energía en los entrenamientos" y "todo el mundo está concentrado, decidido a estar listo para este partido y el resto de la temporada". Preguntado en lo que le ha sorprendido más del equipo, el entrenador destacó "el ambiente" dentro del vestuario: "Todos aportan mucha energía a la pista, sin importar los errores. Lo dan todo para enmendar los errores de los compañeros y jugar como un equipo. Eso es lo que queremos, ser un equipo altruista en ataque y defensa". Sekulic, recién llegado este verano al Palau Blaugrana al igual que once de sus quince jugadores, admitió que necesitará "algo de tiempo para construir la química necesaria para ser competitivos", pese a admitir que deberán "descifrar cómo hacerlo lo antes posible". Sobre el estado de Darío Brizuela, que se retiró de la final de la Lliga Catalana el pasado domingo por una fuerte contusión en la pierna derecha, el técnico respondió que decidirán "entre hoy y mañana por la mañana" si estará disponible, o se unirá a las bajas por lesión de los interiores Tosan Evbuomwan y Yoan Makoundou. Por último, Sekulic auguró un duelo imprevisible este sábado frente al Valencia Basket: "Es difícil de saber qué pasará porque todavía es pretemporada y ninguno de los equipos ha jugado demasiados partidos. No estamos cerca de nuestra cima a nivel físico y táctico, pero por lo que hemos visto juegan un buen baloncesto en defensa y ataque. Será un gran reto".

articles.title: Montero lleva al Olympiacos a la final de la SuperCup
articles.standfirst: Final trepidante en un fabuloso estreno de la nueva competición de la Euroliga
articles.summary: Final trepidante en un fabuloso estreno de la nueva competición de la Euroliga
articles.body: La SuperCup de la Euroliga arrancó a lo grande con un duelo entre los dos últimos campeones de la competición que precisamente son dos de los equipos más y mejor reforzados de la pretemporada. Cosas del dinero turco y, sobre todo, del griego. Ambos equipos se vieron las caras en la pretemporada, con mucho menos rodaje, y en Abu Dabi ofrecieron un gran choque inaugural de esta nueva competición. Aunque era pretemporada, los dos equipos quisieron ganar. Lo buscaron en un partido que fue ganando intensidad de forma paulatina hasta los últimos segundos en los que una canasta de Fournier y un doble fallo de Fenerbahce con un último tiro taponado por Jean Montero, que se adueñó del partido, decidió el partido a favor del Olympiacos, 92-90. Un fabuloso estreno de la SuperCup. El Fenerbahce se quiso hacer pronto con las riendas del partido y adquirió las primeras ventajas en el marcador. Primero pequeñas, 20-24 al final del primer cuarto, y luego más considerables, 24-35 a 6:23 para el descanso. Esa fue la máxima hasta ese momento para el equipo turco, que jugaba con mucha fluidez, principalmente por el trabajo anotador de Shields y Bingham. Al descanso, la ventaja turca se había esfumado y el Olympiacos, de la mano de Fournier, se pegaba con un 43-45. Al partido le faltó una estrella por bando, Milutinov en los griegos y Larkin en los turcos, y se pudo ver el debut europeo en sus nuevos equipos de muchos jugadores, entre ellos de Jean Montero. El dominicano no tardará, si no lo ha hecho ya, en hacer suyo al equipo. Veremos muchos partidos en los que el vigente campeón de la Euroliga juegue a lo que dicte su nuevo base. Tras el descanso, en dos minutos, el Olympiacos ya había empatado el partido, 51-51 con un parcial de 6-0 protagonizado por Donta Hall y sus tiros libres. Dos minutos después un triple de Dorsey ponía por delante al equipo griego. No tardó en reaccionar el 'Fener' que volvió a estirarse corriendo el contraataque, 62-69 cuando quedaban 2:53 y a poco del final del acto recuperó su máxima, 65-76, con un 2+1 de Trent Forrest. Es muy pronto en la temporada pero ya se vio que jugadores nuevos como Braxton Key, en el Fenerbahce, o Mbaye Ndiaye en el Olympiacos van a tener mucho protagonismo por el enorme trabajo que hacen. Olympiacos hizo la goma, se acercaba y se alejaba. En el último periodo perdía 73-81 a 8:40 y logró 8-0 para igualar a 81 dos minutos y medio después. Era el momento de Corey Joseph y sobre todo de Montero a los mandos de los rojos. En el último momento crítico de los griegos, entre Montero, Joseph y Fournier levantaron a a su equipoy lo catapultaron. Robos, intensidad y contraataques para el 90-85 a 2:49 con los griegos jugando su mejor baloncesto. El partido cambió de rumbo otra vez con Shields y Key echñandose a la espalda al 'Fener'. Los turcos igualaron el partido a 90, pero una gran jugada de Fournier, puso al Oly por delante, 92-90, a 53 segundos para el final. En su último ataque, Horton-Tucker falló un tiro de dos, y tras el rebote de ataque de Key, Baldwin no pudo anotar sobre la bocina con un tapón de Montero. Fournier y Montero, los dos mejores del Olympiacos, le dieron la victoria en los últimos segundos y metieron a su equipo en la final. Fournier se fue hasta los 19 puntos, Montero firmó 13 y Joseph hizo 12 en un Olympiacos con 12 rebotes de Donta Hall. En el Fenerbahce, Shields acabó con 18 y Key se fue hasta los 17.

articles.standfirst: El exjugador español era asesor del equipo directivo desde 2022
articles.summary: El exjugador español era asesor del equipo directivo desde 2022
articles.body: José Manuel Calderón ha sido ascendido al cargo de adjunto al gerente general de los Cavaliers. El exjugador español trabajaba en la franquicia de Cleveland desde 2022 como asesor del equipo directivo y ahora sube un peldaño más en la estructura estando más cerca del general manager.
