articles.title: You’re Nuts: What is the Ohio State men’s basketball team’s toughest Big Ten game this season?
articles.summary: Ohio State’s toughest tests look to lie in the oft-floundered month of January. What will be the Buckeyes’ toughest Big Ten game this season?
articles.body:
Welcome back to the most exciting basketball edition of "You're Nuts' in several weeks, because we were gifted a ton of basketball news this week.

From a big schedule drop to a commitment that dominated the headlines on Thursday afternoon, there was no shortage of Ohio State basketball news.

On Wednesday night, the Big Ten released the full men's and women's basketball schedules . Tip times and broadcast information is not available yet, but we now have Ohio State's full 32-game schedule.

The Buckeyes will start conference play on Dec. 2 at Nebraska, and will close Big Ten play on March 7 against Michigan. Ohio State will face Penn State, Iowa, and Michigan twice each, and every other team once.

Then, on Thursday afternoon, Ohio State got its first commitment in the 2027 recruiting class, with Canadian forward Deng Ngor committing to Jake Diebler and the Buckeyes. Ngor is a 6-foot-8, 200-pound forward who is currently ranked No. 95 in the 247Sports composite rankings.

Ngor is one of the fastest risers in the country, as he was unranked at the beginning of the summer, and has now ascended to a four-star recruit and a top-100 prospect.

Last week, Connor and Justin each gave one "hot take" about the Ohio State men's basketball team this season.

Justin said that Justin Pippen will make an All-Big Ten team, citing his elite defense and solid assist numbers. Connor said that the center position is going to be problematic for Ohio State all year long, and broke down why none of the centers on the roster are particularly exciting.

This week, the guys are picking one Big Ten game on the schedule and explaining why it's the toughest conference game of the season. What do you think will be their toughest Big Ten game?

This week's question: What is the Ohio State men's basketball team's toughest Big Ten game this season?

This game at Illinois kicks off the toughest stretch of basketball for Ohio State.

The Buckeyes have to roll into the State Farm Center on a Saturday night and find a way to knock off an elite Illinois team that has Final Four and National Championship potential. Illinois is bringing back three starters from a team that made it to the Final Four last season, and added a double-digit scoring, 6-foot-7 guard in Stefan Vaaks and a five-star freshman guard in Quentin Coleman.

Illinois should be a very well-rounded team this season, with talent on the perimeter as well as near the basket. Senior guard Andrej Stojakovic could wind up as one of the best — or simply the best — player in the Big Ten this season, and on top of all that, it's just really tough to win at Illinois.

This would be a marquee win for Ohio State if they could find a way to pull it off — the Illini will begin the season ranked in the top-10 of the AP Poll and will probably hang out in that range all year long. Beating that caliber of team on their home court in conference play would be a massive boost.

After this game, Ohio State travels to Mackey Arena to play Purdue just three days later. After that, they get Penn State, Michigan State, and Iowa — all at home — over a 9-day stretch. Ohio State would love to win at least three of those games.

Justin: Home against Michigan State – Saturday, Jan. 23

The Buckeyes have a couple of things that stand out when it comes to the schedule, but a stretch of conference games from Jan. 9 to Jan. 30 is the biggest thing. That stretch will likely determine what type of season it will be.

The Michigan State game on Jan. 23 stands out as the most important.

For one, it is at home. Michigan State is going to be a great team next season, and beating them in East Lansing will be almost impossible. The good part is the Buckeyes do not travel to play the Spartans this season, so this will be their one chance to get a win over Michigan State.

It is also in the middle of a home stand against Penn State and Iowa, both teams they will likely be favored against. Penn State definitely, and Iowa likely. So, that is a chance to string together a three-game winning streak in the middle of January, which Ohio State fans know all too well how important that is.

The third reason is that this three-game home stretch is in between three of the toughest road games of the season. Before these three games, the Buckeyes play at Illinois and Purdue, and then after the home stretch plays at Michigan.

So, three wins at home could help that brutal road game stretch. A win over Michigan State will always help the resume.

An NBA executive claims the Indiana Pacers could be a sleeping trade giant heading into the 2026-27 season.

The Pacers and their fanbase knew this past season was going to be a long year once top star Tyrese Haliburton tore his Achilles in the 2025 NBA Finals. However, there are many who believe Indiana is a sleeper team in the Eastern Conference going into the 2026-27 campaign.

The two-time All-Star will be back healthy after sitting out all of the 2025-26 season. They still have talented forward Pascal Siakam . And before last season's trade deadline, they gave up control of their first-round pick in June to the Los Angeles Clippers for underrated impact big man Ivica Zubac . It is a strong trio that will be backed by a solid roster that includes Andrew Nembhard and Aaron Nesmith .

Yet, they may not be done making big moves if the front office believes they are in serious contention to make a second trip to the Finals in three seasons, according to an Eastern Conference executive who spoke to Heavy's Sean Deveney.

"They were kind of quiet this summer, but they made their move with (Zubac). But quiet does not mean they were not busy. I think they were as busy as anyone, getting the lay of the land on what trades might be there for them at the deadline." – Anonymous East Executive

"They were kind of quiet this summer, but they made their move with (Zubac). But quiet does not mean they were not busy. I think they were as busy as anyone, getting the lay of the land on what trades might be there for them at the deadline."

4 big names Indiana Pacers could eventually pursue in a trade

The Pacers are set at their top two frontcourt spots and at point guard. If they do make a big move, it will likely be a deal for a skilled swingman or bench depth. If they looked to add a good small forward or shooting guard to the roster, who could they target?

It's hard to get an idea of how things will look before the 2027 trade deadline. However, there are certain teams that are likely heading toward losing seasons and will be sellers in February. One likely target would be New Orleans Pelicans swingman Trey Murphy III . His scoring ability and athleticism would be a nice fit for the Pacers.

Brooklyn Nets forward Michael Porter Jr. has been on the trade block for months and is sure to be moved at some point. He would give Indiana more size and athleticism in the frontcourt, as well as a dangerous third scoring option.

The Clippers should also be sellers in the winter as they look to get back some of the first-round picks they lost in the Kawhi Leonard salary cap circumvention investigation. So, both Brandon Ingram and Darius Garland could be available to make big impacts for the Pacers.

articles.title: El Madrid de Pedro Martínez sabe sufrir para llegar a la final de la SuperCup
articles.standfirst: Se lleva en la prórroga un partido durísimo ante el Dubai Basketball
articles.summary: Se lleva en la prórroga un partido durísimo ante el Dubai Basketball
articles.body: El que crea que la SuperCup es pretemporada, no sabe de esto. Real Madrid y Dubái se entregaron, como antes Olympiacos y Fenerbahce, en un partidazo que deja la SuperCup como un torneo extraordinario. Ganó el equipo de Pedro Martínez, sufriendo de lo lindo, 95-98 en la prórroga con un tiro de Wright para empatar. El técnico dijo que este torneo le diría dónde está su equipo. Ha tenido que sacar muchas conclusiones. La mala noticia para el técnico catalán es que el Madrid entregó los primeros 17 minutos de partido. La buena es que en apenas tres logró remontar 14 puntos y meterse de lleno en un partido que pintaba muy mal para los blancos. Entre el acierto dubaití y la permisividad en los tiros de la defensa blanca, el Dubái fue construyendo una interesante ventaja que alcanzó su máxima, 36-20, a falta de seis minutos para el descanso. Ya en el primer acto, el equipo de los emiratos había sido mejor, 27-18, pero se vio una mejoría blanca para evitar que el rival hiciera más daño. El equipo de Pascual estaba mucho mejor cuando Shengelia anotó su primer tiro, un triple a 3:33 para el 21-7, el Dubái llevaba 5/5 desde el arco. Luwawu-Cabarrot fue el primero en aparecer en el Madrid, iniciado el segundo cuarto, pero no podía contener al equipo rival que seguía creciendo. Kabengele, a 3:07, anotó una canasta que era el 43-28... y el partido dio un vuelco. De repente Pedro Martínez encontró su cinco idóneo para lo que necesitaba el partido, la vieja guardia formada por Capazzo, Tavares y Deck, más Feliz y Pradilla, muy entonado en ataque. Máxima intensidad defensiva para evitar tiros cómodos rivales y el Madrid secó el ataque dubaití con un parcial de 0-14 que llevó el choque a su máxima igualdad desde el 2-0 inicial de Okobo, 43-42 cuando ambos equipos enfilaban los vestuarios. En la reanudación, el partido empezó a hablar en francés. Okobo anotaba los puntos del Dubái y Luwawu-Cabarrot los del Madrid. Y Maledon cogió luego el testigo de su compañero. Tras un pequeño tirón local, 49-44, el Madrid volvió a igualar fuerzas para empatar primero, 49-49, y lograr su primera ventaja del partido, 50-51 a 6:54. Tavares y Pradilla, que mezclan muy bien, estaban en pista. El coloso de Cabo Verde empató de nuevo el choque, a 56, con su decimocuarto punto del partido. Mucho más sólido, el Madrid logró contrarrestar al Dubái en el tramo final del tercer acto. Los primeros puntos de Campazzo, bien en la dirección, mal en el tiro, llegaron a falta de 37 segundos en dos tiros libres, 63-62, luego una canasta de Andrés Feliz sobre la bocina daba ventaja al Madrid con un cuarto por jugar, 63-64. Tras un par de zarpazos seguidos en forma de triples de Pradilla, que cuajó un gran partido, el Madrid alcanzó su máxima hasta entonces, 67-72. Desde ahí, el guion de nuevo lo pusieron los franceses con Luwawu-Cabarrot muy certero, dos triples, marcando una nueva máxima madridista, 74-81 y Okobo salvando los muebles del Dubái con cinco puntos seguidos, 82-83, a 2:30 para el final, tras un parcial de 10-2. Okobo fue muy protagonista al final. Un canastón suyo neutralizó la ventaja del Madrid obtenida por una canasta de Tavares, 86-85, y luego castigó con una bandeja la pérdida de TCL para poner el 88-85 a falta de 34 segundos para el final. El francés del Madrid enmendó su error con un triple salvador a 25 segundos y el Dubái, con Walkup, fallaba el tiro de la victoria. La primera semifinal amenazó con prórroga. La segunda se iba al tiempo extra. Y en ese tiempo extra, Dubái 0-5 Feliz en los primeros dos minutos para construir una ventaja que era un tesoro, 88-93 y que Campazzo, de tres, hizo aumentar, 88-96. A esas alturas, la desventaja pesaba en el Dubái mientras el Madrid, que acabó mejor, saboreaba el triunfo. Okobo no estaba dispuesto a perder: 5-0 con un triple sore la bocina de posesión y otra canasta a tabla, 93-96 a 57 segundos. Le secundó Wright, con dos tiros libres, para un parcial de 7-0 (95-96 a 18 segundos). El Madrid, que tenía el partido ganado dos minutos y medio, tenía que seguir sufriendo. Dos tiros libres de Luwawu-Cabarrot pusieron el 95-98 y Wright falló el triple para el empate. El final fue el mismo que en la primera semifinal. El Madrid se medirá en la final al Olympiacos. Tavares acabó con 20 puntos y 7 rebotes, Cabarrot casi le calca, 20+6, Deck hizo 15 y Pradilla, 13+7. Junto al Facu, fueron las columnas en las que se apoyó el Madrid en Abu Dabi. En el Dubái, Okobo firmó 24, Bacon, que se retiró lesionado por un golpe, hizo 19 y Wright aportó 12. 95 - Dubai Basketball (27+16+20+25+7): Wright IV (12), Okobo (24), Bacon (19), Blossomgame (4) y Kabengele (10) -cinco inicial-, Anderson (3), Mintz (3), Bertans (-), Diakité (5), Shengelia (11), Petrusev (-) y Walkup (4). 98 - Real Madrid (18+24+22+24+10): Campazzo (5), Feliz (10), Deck (15), Okeke (4) y Tavares (20) -cinco inicial-, Shulga (-), Luwawu-Cabarrot (20), Pradilla (13), Abalde (-), Maledon (4), Jantunen (5) y Sarr (2).

articles.title: New NBA Rumors on Brandon Miller, Ausar Thompson, Brandin Podziemski & Rookie Contract Extensions
articles.summary: Less than two weeks away from the start of training camps around the NBA, several players from the 2023 draft class could get new contracts in the near-future.
articles.body:
Less than two weeks away from the start of training camps around the NBA, several players from the 2023 draft class could get new contracts in the near-future.

Appearing on Friday's episode of NBA Today , ESPN's Shams Charania explained Brandon Miller of the Charlotte Hornets and Ausar Thompson of the Detroit Pistons will start to have "more and more conversations" with their clubs in the "upcoming days and weeks."

Charania added Thompson's situation, in particular, has "optimism" with the Pistons. He also noted cited Brandin Podziemski (Golden State Warriors), Cason Wallace (Oklahoma City Thunder), Jaime Jaquez Jr. (Milwaukee Bucks) and Anthony Black (Orlando Magic) as players to "keep an eye on) as far as rookie extensions go.

5 NBA Stars Who Could Dominate Trade Rumors 🤔

Victor Wembanyama, Keyonte George and Amen Thompson are the only first-round picks from the '23 class that have signed extensions thus far.

From that trio, Wembanyama is the only who received a max extension projected to be worth $252 million over five years. The San Antonio Spurs star opted not to go for the supermax that could have pushed the total value to $303 million to give the club financial flexibility in the future.

Using Keith Smith of Spotrac's projected contracts for the other members of the 2023 draft, Miller is likely to be the highest-paid player with an estimated deal worth $200 million over five years.

Miller has some added leverage over the Hornets after they traded LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges early in the offseason. Those deals indicated the club views Miller and Kon Knueppel as their top two players going forward.

The Hornets are projected to be $62.4 million under the tax for the 2027-28 season with their savings from trading Ball's contract.

Podziemski's development over his first three seasons has made him an invaluable piece for the Golden State Warriors. He set career-highs in scoring average (13.8 points) and field-goal percentage (45.5) last season.

It also helps Podziemski's leverage that he is one of the few young contributors on a Warriors roster led by mid- to late-30s veterans like Stephen Curry, Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler.

Ausar Thompson's contract comes at an interesting time for the Pistons, who are still trying to figure out a solution to their ongoing standoff with Jalen Duren. He remains a limited offensive player, but is also coming off a 2025-26 season in which he was named to the All-Defensive first team and finished third in Defensive Player of the Year voting.

Jaquez is another interesting extension candidate because it's unclear how the Bucks feel about him after acquiring him from the Miami Heat as part of the Giannis Antetokounmpo trade.

The 25-year-old Jaquez has been very good primarily off the bench over the past three years in Miami, but he might be used in a starting role for Milwaukee that could change his production.

Oklahoma City seemed to signal a Wallace extension could be coming after shedding money after trading Lu Dort, Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins. Wallace shares a similar profile to Thompson in that their impact is primarily felt on defense, though the former has been a better three-point shooter with a 37.4 percent success rate.

The deadline for players to sign rookie extensions is 6 p.m. ET on Oct. 19. All 30 training camps will open on Sept. 29, which could be when we start to see more movement on these contract talks.

articles.title: Kawhi Leonard Thanks Clippers Fans With Tribute Video After Trade to Raptors Ahead of NBA Season
articles.summary: Kawhi Leonard said his goodbye to fans of the Los Angeles Clippers after his trade to the Toronto Raptors became official.
articles.body:
Kawhi Leonard said his goodbye to fans of the Los Angeles Clippers after his trade to the Toronto Raptors became official.

"I truly appreciate your unwavering support during both the highs and lows," he wrote Friday on Instagram. "Thank you, Clip Nation. ✋🏾"

5 NBA Stars Who Could Dominate Trade Rumors 🤔

Especially in light of recent events, a lot of Clippers fans might be happy the organization is finally turning the page from an era that started during the 2019 offseason.

Los Angeles made a solitary appearance in the Western Conference Finals and didn't get further than that after pairing Leonard and Paul George together. Injuries to one or both stars doomed the team's efforts to win a title.

Compounding matters, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander blossomed into a two-time MVP and NBA champion after the Clippers traded him to the Oklahoma City Thunder as part of the deal to land George.

Then came a full accounting of the efforts that led Leonard to signing with the team. Due to "a pattern of misconduct and multiple significant rules violations" in the words of the NBA, L.A. had to forfeit five first-round picks and pay a $30 million among other punishments.

Leonard's seven years in Southern California were a disappointment in terms of what the Clippers achieved, and now his legacy will be the penalties that complicate their transition to a different phase.

A brief goodbye message and a 13-second highlight reel feel like an appropriate way to make an exit given Kawhi's understated persona and what became a complicated divorce.

Now, the question is what kind of tribute the seven-time All-Star will get when the Raptors play the Clippers on Nov. 2 at Intuit Dome.

articles.standfirst: El técnico analizó la trabajada victoria de su equipo ante el Dubai Basketball
articles.summary: El técnico analizó la trabajada victoria de su equipo ante el Dubai Basketball
articles.body: Pedro Martínez ya tiene su debut en un partido oficial. Le quedan más, porque la SuperCup es sólo el arranque de la temporada, pero ya sabe que las victorias las van a tener que trabajar. El Madrid sufrió para ganar al Dubái, lo hizo en la prórroga, que jugó mejor, pero a la que llegó con un triple de Luwawu-Cabarrot. Jugará la final ante el Olympiacos este sábado a partir de las 19.00 horas. El técnico explicaba así el partido: "Ha sido un choque muy difícil. Esperábamos este tipo de partidos, muy físicos, contra un buen equipo, con una buena defensa. En la primera mitad, nos dominaron en el ritmo, en la defensa, y tenemos mucho que progresar para ganar y tener una buena sensación. Afortunadamente, terminamos bien el segundo cuarto, y en la segunda mitad tuvimos una gran opción para ganar, con 2 o 3 minutos hasta el final, pero cometimos algunos errores.Tenemos que seguir trabajando para mejorar". El técnico catalán se mostraba satisfecho por la reacción de sus jugadores cuando el partido se complicaba: "Hemos de estar contentos pero no podemos pensar que vamos a ganar los partidos con facilidad. Hemos sufrido, el equipo ha demostrado capacidad de sufrimiento, ha demostrado personalidad. Cuando ganas en la prórroga es un cara o cruz, hoy ha salido cara, y hemos de estar contentos del esfuerzo que hemos hecho, sobre todo por lo mal que hemos empezado para volver al partido. Hemos llegado a perder 16 puntos en el segundo cuarto, y aunque es verdad que en pretemporada es normal estos parciales adversos y a favor, hemos tenido la capacidad para volver". En la rueda de prensa tras el partido, Martínez analizó algunos puntos más tácticos: "Creo que hemos tirado bien de tres puntos, pero poco. Tiramos poco, tenemos que mejorar, ser capaces de encontrar más tiros de tres puntos de los que hemos encontrado hoy. En defensa creo que debemos de ser críticos, y ser más duros, ser más físicos, estar más en las líneas de pase, defender mejor las situaciones de uno contra uno. Hoy no hemos estado sólidos. Pero es normal en el momento en el que estamos. Si queremos mejorar, tenemos que trabajar".

articles.title: Pelle Larsson, Heat Agree to Contract Extension, Details and Salary Cap Impact Revealed
articles.summary: The Miami Heat and guard Pelle Larsson preempted his restricted free agency by agreeing to a long-term extension, according to ESPN's Shams Charania.
articles.body:
The Miami Heat and guard Pelle Larsson preempted his restricted free agency by agreeing to a long-term extension, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Larsson, who was in the final season of his rookie deal, will make $60 million over four years, and the final year (2030-31) is a mutual option.

The Swedish international saw his role with Miami significantly increase last year. He appeared in 70 games and saw his minutes climb from 14.2 to 26.4. He was sixth on the team in scoring (11.4 points) and fourth in assists (3.4).

Larsson still projects as a backup for the Heat following their busy offseason. Tim Hardaway Jr. and Andrew Wiggins are likely to start at the 2 and 3, respectively, and Klay Thompson will be a reserve at both positions.

Being proactive a year out from Larsson potentially hitting the market makes sense.

The Heat have oriented their present and future around Giannis Antetokounmpo, who can opt out in 2027, and Bam Adebayo, who can do the same in 2028. Keeping those two together will be expensive and limit what Miami can do elsewhere on the roster.

Having Larsson on the books through at least 2029-30 gives the front office some more cost certainty and ensures a solid role player will stick around for the next few years.

Larsson may instead prove to be a trade asset whose salary can be aggregated to make an upgrade to the squad. That's another luxury the new-look Heat don't exactly possess.

articles.title: Lakers Reportedly Projected to Reach $30B Valuation Within 10 Years After Kushner, Iger Sale
articles.summary: Within a decade, the record-setting price for the Los Angeles Lakers could look like a bargain.
articles.body:
Within a decade, the record-setting price for the Los Angeles Lakers could look like a bargain.

Jessica Toonkel and Mark Maurer of the Wall Street Journal reported the investment firm led by Josh Kusher is projecting the Lakers could be worth $30 billion inside another 10 years.

Kusher and Bob Iger are at the front of the ownership group that agreed to purchase the Lakers from Mark Walter for $12.5 billion.

5 NBA Stars Who Could Dominate Trade Rumors 🤔

Landing Spots for Top 5 Unsigned NBA Free Agents 🏀

Kushner is seeking minority investors and as part of that made an aggressive pitch in terms of how the NBA's and Lakers' revenues may continue to climb.

According to Toonkel and Maurer, he cited the possibility for expansion. The NBA is exploring the addition of franchises in Seattle and Las Vegas, but no concrete plans have been made.

The league continues to widen its footprint outside of the United States as well. More international players than ever are thriving, and commissioner Adam Silver has set a target of 2027-28 to launch the NBA's Europe-based competition.

Then there's the money from media rights. The Wall Street Journal reported Kushner's investment firm is planning for the NBA's national TV money to double when the negotiating window next opens. In 2024, it collectively secured $77 billion over an 11-year period.

Concerns over the sports TV bubble popping span decades, yet the money continues to flow. Nothing is appointment viewing quite like live sports, and leagues use that to their advantage.

The wide embrace of streaming services — the NBA has games on Peacock and Prime Video — is a sign of the larger shifts in television, though.

The regional network model, which had been successful for a long time, is no longer sustainable , either, and pivoting to individual streaming deals isn't as lucrative .

Maybe the NBA will have enough leverage to double its media rights down the road. Basing a future evaluation of the Lakers on that could be a risky bet.

articles.title: Ausar Thompson, Pistons Reportedly Agree to Contract Extension, Details and Updated Salary Cap
articles.summary: The Detroit Pistons locked in another piece of their young core by agreeing to a five-year, $155 million extension with wing Ausar Thompson, according to ESPN's Shams Charania.
articles.body:
The Detroit Pistons locked in another piece of their young core by agreeing to a five-year, $155 million extension with wing Ausar Thompson, according to ESPN's Shams Charania.

Thompson's deal is fully guaranteed, per Charania.

The Pistons currently have $183.4 million in total salary cap allocations for 2026-27, per Spotrac .

5 NBA Stars Who Could Dominate Trade Rumors 🤔

Thompson's twin brother, Amen, previously signed a $208 million contract extension with the Houston Rockets. They're the first pair of brothers in NBA history to receive a $100 million deal, per Charania.

Thompson was still under contract for one more season and would've been eligible for restricted free agency in 2027. It's doubtful he would've left the Motor City anytime soon, but there was no reason to wait on his next contract when he has proven to be such a valuable contributor.

The 23-year-old finished third in the Defensive Player of the Year voting for 2025-26 after leading the NBA in steals at 2.0 per game and averaging 0.9 blocks.

Thompson's work on the perimeter helped to set the tone as the Pistons posted the league's second-best defensive rating (108.9), per NBA.com .

Beyond seeing the team become a contender again, fans in Detroit have reveled in watching a brand of basketball that mirrors the franchise's two most successful periods.

The "Bad Boys" era from the late 1980s to the early 1990s and then the run of six straight Eastern Conference Finals appearances from 2003-08 were fueled by a physical style that ground down the Pistons' opponents.

That identity has returned under coach J.B. Bickerstaff, and Thompson has relished his role as a defensive stopper.

"You know how people have offensive modes where they feel like they're on fire? I feel like I have defensive modes like that," he told The Athletic's Hunter Patterson in February. "So when I get in modes like that I'm like, 'Yeah, this guy's not scoring. Or it's going to be really hard.'"

Thompson also emphasized his versatility.

"I think I'm best in a lot of situations," he said. "I think if you need me to be a point-of-attack (defender), pick up to slow down the clock or get over screens, I can do that. If you put me off-ball and have me as a roamer, I'm really good at that because I can block shots and be in the passing lanes. Those are my two strongest (attributes)."

Thompson's limitations on the other end of the floor will always be a consideration when projecting his overall value. His scoring average in 2025-26 was just 9.9 points, and he attempted 24 three-pointers across the entire year.

The lack of shooting range becomes a bigger issue in the playoffs, when opposing coaches more frequently target and exploit individual matchups.

In terms of looking at the roster as a whole, the Pistons have the added challenge of figuring out who to prioritize and how much they're willing to pay with so many young players on the same timeline.

Fresh off making his first All-Star appearance, Jalen Duren is a restricted free agent and locked in a tense contract battle. Isaiah Stewart got traded two years out from his free agency in 2028. Ron Holland II will be due a new contract by then too.

With Cade Cunningham already making $53.8 million a year, the front office has to be judicious about its spending. There's a reason so many teams work diligently to avoid the second apron of the luxury tax.

Being proactive in re-signing him is a sign of how important Detroit views Thompson toward achieving its long-term goals.

articles.title: Pistons, Ausar Thompson reportedly agree to 5-year, $155 million rookie-scale contract extension
articles.summary: Thompson was named to the NBA All-Defensive First Team in his third season.
articles.body:
The Detroit Pistons and forward Ausar Thompson have agreed to a five-year, $155 million contract extension, ESPN's Shams Charania reports . The deal has not yet been officially announced by the team.

Thompson, 23, was named to the NBA's All-Defensive First Team and finished third in Defensive Player of the Year voting in his third season as Detroit finished with the top record in the Eastern Conference at 60-22.

The Pistons' 2023 first-round pick (No. 5 overall) out of Overtime Elite Academy in Atlanta , Thompson led the league with an average of 2 steals per game with 9.9 points, 5.7 rebounds, 3.1 assists and 0.9 blocks in 73 games, while shooting 52% from the floor.

Signing Thompson to an extension was an underlying priority for the Pistons during the offseason, which was a primary reason why the team has declined to sign restricted free-agent center Jalen Duren to the five-year max contract extension he's seeking.

Additionally, many observers questioned why Detroit and president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon failed to make a blockbuster addition to the roster while several Eastern Conference rivals improved themselves dramatically.

The Pistons had until Oct. 19 to sign Thompson to an extension. He is set to make $11.1 million in the final year of his rookie contract.

Thompson's twin brother, Amen, signed a five-year, $208 million extensio n with the Houston Rockets earlier this month. He was selected one spot earlier than Ausar in the 2023 NBA Draft and was viewed as the better scorer. (Amen averaged 18.3 points per game last season.)

Now, the brothers have agreed to contracts worth a combined $363 million, becoming the highest-paid pair of twins in NBA history .

Ausar Thompson extension took priority for Pistons over Jalen Duren deal

Duren, 22, is eligible for a max extension of five years and $287 million after being named Third Team All-NBA last season. The 6-foot-10 center averaged 19.5 points and 10.5 rebounds per game, while also being named to the Eastern Conference All-Star team for the first time.

However, the Pistons do not want to pay Duren more than $50 million per season, especially after he underperformed badly in the playoffs, averaging 10.8 points and 8.5 rebounds. Detroit has reportedly offered Duren a contract in the five-year, $190 million range, according to The Athletic .

Because of the contract stalemate, Duren is reportedly considering taking a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer and becoming an unrestricted free agent after the coming season. Duren has until Oct. 1 to accept that offer.

In the meantime, he and his representation are pushing for a trade to the Sacramento Kings , one of the teams willing to sign the center to a max contract, according to reports . However, the Pistons apparently are not interested in making a deal.

articles.title: Mets Top Prospect Keeps Slugging After Triple-A Promotion
articles.summary: The Mets added plenty of prospects at the deadline, and Jefferson Rojas is a name to watch.
articles.body:
The New York Mets made multiple moves at the trade deadline, and in the process they basically revamped their farm system, which was depleted by multiple successful promotions this year. They acquired 11 prospects in the process, and one in particular stands out.

That would be infielder Jefferson Rojas, who's been showing signs of "coming soon" rather than being "out on the horizon." The 21-year old Rojas was promoted to Triple-A recently, and he responded by hitting home runs in his first three games with Syracuse, according to Jesse Borek of MLB.com

Rojas went 7-for-12 in the process, and this was after hitting nine homers in 29 games for Double-A Binghamton. Triple-A teams typically have far more ex-major leaguers on their rosters, but this doesn't seem to be making a bit of difference to Rojas so far.

The infielder has been facing some of those hurlers, including Brian Keller, Alan Ranger and Tucker Davidson . They're not recognizable names, but it's the level of competition that matters here.

The Triple-A promotion also comes with better data collection that should help the Mets in their evaluation. He's put eight balls in play at an exit velocity of over 100 mph, per Borek, and that's big league stuff.

He also has 20 steals to go with 27 homers this year with three different teams, and the extra exposure is undoubtedly helping. The last time a Met had a minor league campaign with that many steals and homers was Ronny Mauricio back in 2022, but Mauricio's career has fizzled at this point.

If Rojas's story sounds familiar to Mets fans, it should. The Mets promoted outfielders Carson Benge and A.J. Ewing to Triple-A late last season, and Ewing in particular had noteworthy success. Benge struggled at the next level , but that certainly didn't stop him this year, as he's become a lineup staple who's got a legit chance to hit 20 homers.

The Mets may be thinking along the same lines with Rojas. According to Borek, he's played multiple infield positions, and the Mets are already looking at which position might be right for him.

The decision so far is third base, which would be an especially juicy storyline given that current third baseman Bo Bichette as an opt-out five days after the World Series ends. It's yet another development to follow in what looks like an even busier offseason for the Mets.

articles.title: Charlotte Bobcats jersey history No. 2 Dontell Jefferson 2008-2009
articles.summary: Dontell Jefferson played in just NBA games during his career, all of which came with the Charlotte Bobcats during the 2008-2009 season.
articles.body:
After playing two seasons of college basketball at Arkansas, Dontell Jefferson grinded his way into the NBA as an undrafted free agent. At age 25, Jefferson earned his first opportunity in the NBA after the Charlotte Bobcats signed him from the D-League at the end of March. Having signed a deal with less than a month to play in the regular season, Jefferson made just six appearances for the Bobcats, averaging 4.8 points, two rebounds, 1.5 assists, 0.7 steals and 0.2 blocks in 14 minutes per game.

Unfortunately for Jefferson, he wouldn't find another opportunity in the NBA afterward. That said, the former Razorbacks guard did play for different teams abroad, including some in Canada, Latvia and Saudi Arabia.
